items.stem: An internal assistant calls a remote MCP server. The server must record which employee asked for each action. Which change meets the constraint?
options: Use one shared service key, and add the employee name to the prompt.
Send each user's OAuth token in authorization_token for that server.
Send one shared OAuth token for all users, and route all calls through a logging proxy.
Set the anthropic-workspace-id header to the employee's team workspace.
items.rationale: The server checks a bearer token that names the signed-in user. A name typed into a prompt cannot prove who asked (Inference).
items.trap: A shared key with a name in the prompt looks like attribution, but the system cannot verify a name that the user typed (Inference).

items.stem: A workload runs on Claude Platform on AWS. The security team needs IAM to control each caller, and the workload has no user consent flow. Which change meets both constraints?
options: Store a long-lived API key in the code, and skip IAM policies.
Add an OAuth consent screen for each user before each call.
Sign with SigV4 from one shared role for all callers, and log each request ID in a second store.
Enable outbound web identity federation, sign with SigV4, and scope IAM to the workspace ARN.
items.rationale: Outbound web identity federation is disabled by default, so requests fail until it is enabled. An IAM policy on the workspace ARN then limits each caller.
items.trap: An OAuth consent screen looks like user control, but Claude Platform on AWS does not support OAuth.

items.stem: On the Claude API, two tenants must not share prompt caches or API keys. The team also wants a separate monthly spend limit for each tenant. Which two changes meet both constraints?
options: Use one workspace for both tenants, and name each tenant in a header.
Rename the Default Workspace to the first tenant, then archive it later.
Create one workspace per tenant, and scope each tenant key to its workspace.
Set a monthly spend limit on each tenant workspace.
items.rationale: Prompt caches stay isolated by workspace on the Claude API. Each new workspace can also have its own spend limit.
items.trap: A tenant header in one workspace looks like isolation, but both tenants then share one prompt cache and one spend limit.
